subproblem.title: Compactly supported cutoff equal to 1 on the cone X ∩ B₁(0) and vanishing on Q outside B̄_δ(0)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection p_Q (Q.starProjection), and let δ > 0. Then there is a continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ (an element of CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Euclid P) ℝ) such that 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 everywhere, f(y) = 1 whenever 2|p_Q y| < |y| and |y| < 1 (that is, on X ∩ B₁(0) with X = {y : 2|p_Q y| < |y|}), and f(y) = 0 whenever y ∈ Q and |y| > δ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → ∃ f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Euclid P) ℝ, (∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) ∧ (∀ y, f y ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ y : Euclid P, 2 * ‖Q.starProjection y‖ < ‖y‖ → ‖y‖ < 1 → f y = 1) ∧ ∀ y ∈ Q, δ < ‖y‖ → f y = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof (the test function f = φχ with properties (a) and (b)), with the supplied parameter s chosen as s := δ/4, so that the supplied radius 4s equals δ. Notation: p_Q := Q.starProjection (the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto Q, a continuous linear map), |·| the Euclidean norm.

1. Definition. Put s := δ/4 > 0. For y ∈ ℝ^P let h(y) := (3/4)|y| − |p_Q y|, φ(y) := max(0, min(1, 1 + h(y)/s)), χ(y) := max(0, min(1, 2 − |y|)) and f(y) := φ(y)·χ(y).
2. Continuity. y ↦ |y| is continuous, and y ↦ |p_Q y| is continuous because p_Q is a continuous linear map. Constants, sums, differences, constant multiples, division by the nonzero constant s, min, max and products of continuous real-valued functions are continuous. Hence f is continuous.
3. Compact support. If |y| > 2, then 2 − |y| < 0 < 1, so min(1, 2 − |y|) = 2 − |y| and χ(y) = max(0, 2 − |y|) = 0, whence f(y) = φ(y)·0 = 0. Thus f vanishes outside the closed ball B̄₂(0), which is compact because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional (proper). Therefore f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro with K = closedBall 0 2), and f together with the proofs of steps 2–3 is an element of CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Euclid P) ℝ.
4. Bounds 0 ≤ f ≤ 1. For every real a, max(0, min(1, a)) lies in [0, 1]: it is ≥ 0 by max, and ≤ 1 since 0 ≤ 1 and min(1, a) ≤ 1. Hence 0 ≤ φ(y) ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ χ(y) ≤ 1. Therefore f(y) = φ(y)χ(y) ≥ 0 as a product of nonnegative numbers, and f(y) = φ(y)χ(y) ≤ φ(y)·1 = φ(y) ≤ 1, using χ(y) ≤ 1 and φ(y) ≥ 0.
5. Property (a): f = 1 on X ∩ B₁(0). Let 2|p_Q y| < |y| and |y| < 1. Then |p_Q y| < |y|/2, so h(y) = (3/4)|y| − |p_Q y| > (3/4)|y| − |y|/2 = |y|/4 ≥ 0. Hence h(y)/s ≥ 0 (as s > 0), so 1 + h(y)/s ≥ 1, min(1, 1 + h(y)/s) = 1 and φ(y) = max(0, 1) = 1. Moreover 2 − |y| > 1, so min(1, 2 − |y|) = 1 and χ(y) = 1. Therefore f(y) = 1·1 = 1.
6. Property (b): f = 0 on Q outside B̄_δ(0). Let y ∈ Q with |y| > δ. Since y ∈ Q, p_Q y = y (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), so h(y) = (3/4)|y| − |y| = −|y|/4 and h(y)/s = −|y|/(4s) = −|y|/δ. Because |y| > δ > 0 we have |y|/δ > 1, so 1 + h(y)/s = 1 − |y|/δ < 0. Then min(1, 1 + h(y)/s) = 1 + h(y)/s < 0 and φ(y) = max(0, 1 + h(y)/s) = 0, hence f(y) = 0·χ(y) = 0.
7. Steps 3–6 show that f satisfies all four required properties: 0 ≤ f, f ≤ 1, f(y) = 1 whenever 2‖p_Q y‖ < ‖y‖ and ‖y‖ < 1, and f(y) = 0 whenever y ∈ Q and δ < ‖y‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: f is continuous, vanishes outside B̄₂(0), and takes values in [0, 1], so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
If 2|p_Q y| < |y| < 1 then h(y) > |y|/4 ≥ 0 gives φ(y) = 1, and χ(y) = 1, so f(y) = 1.
If y ∈ Q and |y| > δ then p_Q y = y, so 1 + h(y)/s = 1 − |y|/δ < 0, φ(y) = 0 and f(y) = 0.

audit.reason: The explicit construction with s = δ/4 proves continuity, compact support, both bounds, and both required value conditions. Orthogonal projection instances resolve for arbitrary Euclid P submodules. The proof establishes exactly the stated existential proposition without dependencies or circularity.

subproblem.title: Hⁿ-measure of a closed ball in an n-dimensional linear subspace
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim Q = n. Then for every real r ≥ 0, Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_r(0)) = rⁿ ωₙ, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure) and ωₙ = unitBallVolume n = Lⁿ(B₁(0) ⊂ ℝⁿ); in ℝ≥0∞: μHE[n](Q ∩ closedBall 0 r) = ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ) · unitBallVolume n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 ≤ r → μHE[n] ((Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) * unitBallVolume n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof ("An orthonormal basis of Q gives a linear isometry j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with range Q, and j(B̄_r(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_r(0). Since Hⁿ is isometry invariant and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_r(0)) = Lⁿ(B̄_r(0)) = rⁿ ωₙ"), stated for every r ≥ 0 and every n. Notation: ℝᵐ = Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), Hⁿ = μHE[n], ωₙ = unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) (definition in GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean).

1. Orthonormal coordinates on Q. Since finrank ℝ Q = n, the subspace Q (an inner product space) has an orthonormal basis b indexed by Fin n; for instance take Mathlib's stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q and reindex it along finCongr applied to the hypothesis finrank ℝ Q = n. Its coordinate map b.repr : Q ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝⁿ is a linear isometry equivalence.
2. The isometry j. Let ι := Q.subtypeₗᵢ : Q →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ^P be the inclusion and j := ι ∘ b.repr.symm : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P. As a composition of two isometries, j is an isometry. For every v ∈ ℝⁿ, j v ∈ Q and ‖j v‖ = ‖b.repr.symm v‖ = ‖v‖ (both maps preserve norms).
3. j(B̄_r(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_r(0). If ‖v‖ ≤ r then j v ∈ Q and ‖j v‖ = ‖v‖ ≤ r, so j v ∈ Q ∩ B̄_r(0). Conversely let y ∈ Q with ‖y‖ ≤ r and put v := b.repr ⟨y, y ∈ Q⟩ ∈ ℝⁿ. Then ‖v‖ = ‖⟨y, _⟩‖ = ‖y‖ ≤ r (b.repr preserves norms and the norm on Q is the ambient norm), and j v = ι(b.repr.symm (b.repr ⟨y, _⟩)) = y. Hence the two sets are equal.
4. Isometry invariance. By Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image (μHE[d](f '' s) = μHE[d](s) for every isometry f and every set s), Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_r(0)) = Hⁿ(j(B̄_r(0))) = μHE[n](closedBall (0 : ℝⁿ) r).
5. Hⁿ on ℝⁿ is Lebesgue measure. By Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n, μHE[n] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). So Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_r(0)) = volume(closedBall (0 : ℝⁿ) r).
6. Haar scaling. volume on ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure and finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Mathlib Measure.addHaar_closedBall (stated for all r ≥ 0, with no nontriviality hypothesis) gives volume(closedBall 0 r) = ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) * volume(ball (0 : ℝⁿ) 1).
7. Conclusion. volume(ball (0 : ℝⁿ) 1) is by definition unitBallVolume n. Combining steps 4–6, μHE[n](Q ∩ closedBall 0 r) = ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) * unitBallVolume n. ∎
proof_key_steps: An orthonormal basis of Q indexed by Fin n gives a linear isometry j = Q.subtypeₗᵢ ∘ b.repr.symm : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with j(B̄_r(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_r(0).
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
Haar scaling volume(B̄_r(0)) = ofReal(rⁿ)·volume(B₁(0)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, finrank ℝⁿ = n) and volume(B₁(0)) = unitBallVolume n.

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree. Orthonormal coordinates identify the closed ball in Q with its Euclidean counterpart; isometry invariance and Haar scaling prove the formula. The pinned closed-ball lemma covers n = 0 and r = 0 without an extra nontriviality hypothesis.

subproblem.title: Small-scale upper bound for Hⁿ(M ∩ η_{x,r}⁻¹(U)) from a test function dominating 1_U at an approximate tangent point
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), x ∈ ℝ^P, and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P which is the approximate tangent space of M at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q). Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be a measurable set and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) with f ≥ 0 everywhere and f ≥ 1 on U. If t ∈ [0, ∞] satisfies ofReal(∫_Q f dHⁿ) < t, then for all sufficiently small r > 0 (eventually in 𝓝[>] 0), Hⁿ(M ∩ η_{x,r}⁻¹(U)) ≤ t·rⁿ, where η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) is SimonGMT's blowUpMap x r.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Euclid P) ℝ), μHE[n] M ≠ ∞ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → MeasurableSet U → (∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) → (∀ y ∈ U, 1 ≤ f y) → ∀ t : ℝ≥0∞, ENNReal.ofReal (∫ y in (Q : Set (Euclid P)), f y ∂μHE[n]) < t → ∀ᶠ r in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μHE[n] (M ∩ Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r ⁻¹' U) ≤ t * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0, 3 (second half), 4, 5 and 6 of the supplied proof, carried out for an arbitrary measurable set U and an arbitrary nonnegative test function f ∈ C_c with f ≥ 1 on U (the supplied proof uses U = X ∩ B₁(0) and its explicit f). Notation: η_r := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η_r(z) = r⁻¹(z − x); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; L := ∫ y in Q, f y ∂Hⁿ (Bochner integral for Hⁿ⌞Q); I(r) := ∫ y in η_r '' M, f y ∂Hⁿ. The sibling blowup_scaling states: for r > 0 and every S ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(η_r '' S) = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) * Hⁿ(S).

1. Case t = ∞. For r > 0 we have rⁿ > 0, so ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ) ≠ 0 and t * ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ) = ∞ (ENNReal.top_mul); the inequality then holds trivially. Since Ioi 0 ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin), the claim holds. From now on t ≠ ∞.
2. The limit is below t. Since f ≥ 0 everywhere, L ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg). As L ≥ 0 and t ≠ ∞, the hypothesis ENNReal.ofReal L < t is equivalent to L < t.toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_iff_lt_toReal). So L < t.toReal.
3. Eventually I(r) < t.toReal. The second component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, applied to f, says I(r) → L as r → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. Since (−∞, t.toReal) is a neighbourhood of L, the set {r : I(r) < t.toReal} belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Tendsto.eventually with gt_mem_nhds). Intersecting with Ioi 0 ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, it suffices to fix r with r > 0 and I(r) < t.toReal and to prove Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U)) ≤ t * ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ).
4. Finiteness and integrability. Put S := η_r '' M. By blowup_scaling, Hⁿ(S) = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) * Hⁿ(M), a product of two finite factors (ENNReal.ofReal is never ∞ and Hⁿ(M) ≠ ∞ by hypothesis), so Hⁿ(S) ≠ ∞. Hence ν := Hⁿ.restrict S is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict), hence locally finite and finite on compact sets, and the continuous compactly supported f is ν-integrable (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.integrable). Since f ≥ 0 as well, ENNReal.ofReal (I(r)) = ∫⁻ y, ENNReal.ofReal (f y) ∂ν (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal).
5. Comparison. For every y, U.indicator 1 y ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (f y): if y ∈ U then f y ≥ 1, so ENNReal.ofReal (f y) ≥ 1 (ENNReal.one_le_ofReal); if y ∉ U the left side is 0. Since U is measurable, Hⁿ(S ∩ U) = ν(U) (Measure.restrict_apply gives ν(U) = Hⁿ(U ∩ S)) = ∫⁻ U.indicator 1 dν (lintegral_indicator_one) ≤ ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal ∘ f dν (lintegral_mono) = ENNReal.ofReal (I(r)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (t.toReal) (I(r) < t.toReal and monotonicity of ofReal) = t (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, t ≠ ∞). So Hⁿ(S ∩ U) ≤ t.
6. Rescaling the set. (η_r '' M) ∩ U = η_r '' (M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U)) (Set.image_inter_preimage). By blowup_scaling applied to the set M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U), Hⁿ(S ∩ U) = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) * Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U)). With step 5: ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) * Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U)) ≤ t.
7. Conclusion. Since rⁿ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ) * ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) = ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ · r⁻¹ ^ n) = ENNReal.ofReal ((r · r⁻¹)ⁿ) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, mul_pow, r ≠ 0). Hence Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U)) = ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ) * (ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) * Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹(U))) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ) * t = t * ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ), using step 6 and monotonicity of multiplication in ℝ≥0∞. This holds for every r in the set chosen in step 3, which belongs to 𝓝[>] 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: If t = ∞ the bound is trivial for r > 0; otherwise ofReal(L) < t with L = ∫_Q f ≥ 0 gives L < t.toReal.
HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt gives ∫_{η_r(M)} f → L, so ∫_{η_r(M)} f < t.toReal for all small r > 0.
blowup_scaling gives Hⁿ(η_r(M)) < ∞, so f is integrable for Hⁿ⌞η_r(M) and Hⁿ(η_r(M) ∩ U) ≤ ofReal(∫_{η_r(M)} f) ≤ t because 1_U ≤ ofReal ∘ f.
η_r(M) ∩ U = η_r(M ∩ η_r⁻¹U) and blowup_scaling give ofReal(r⁻ⁿ)·Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹U) ≤ t; multiplying by ofReal(rⁿ) yields Hⁿ(M ∩ η_r⁻¹U) ≤ t·ofReal(rⁿ).

audit.reason: All hypotheses match the prose. Scaling supplies finite restricted measure and integrability without requiring M measurable. Tangent convergence, the measurable indicator comparison, image/preimage identity, and positive scaling cancellation give the exact eventual bound. The t = ∞ case is handled correctly; its only child dependency is blowup_scaling.
